full_judgment:
3. Raja Rajendra Narayan Roy Bahadur, the Zaminder of Bhawal Estate, in the beginning of the 20th century, endowed 20 (twenty) Bighas of land, the boundaries being, in the East-West and North permanent concrete (pucca) Demarcation Pillars of the Government, in the south Government Land and the main Dhakeswari Mandir premises, (situated previously) within Dhakeswari Mohal Khatian No. 2168 under Dhaka Sadar Police Station and presently under Police Station Chawkbazar, District-Dhaka, as Debottar property in the name of the Petitioner No. 1. Sree Sree Dhakeswari Mata, and continued seva-puja of the Petitioner No. 1. After demise of Raja Rajendra Narayan Roy, his three sons, namely; 1) Kumar Ranendra Narayan Roy, 2) Romendra Narayan Roy and 3) Rabindra Narayan Roy endowed the said property in the name of the Petitioner No. 1, Sree Sree Dhakeswari Mata vide Registered `Vogartho Kabuliyat' Deed No.1374 dated 4-4-1908.The deed entrusted the property to the Sebayet, Sree Protab Chandra Chakroborty and other Mudis and Servicemen Praja, living in the said 20 (twenty) Bighas land in 3(Three) specific Shaham of land on condition that they would jointly share the duty of daily Seva-puja, Rituals and Services of the Temple. 

 7. After CS record, the then East Bengal encountered a huge turmoil with the movement of Indian independence which resulted into the partition of India and creation of Pakistan. In this stream of turbulence, the Mudis and the Servicemen Proja/Occupants of the Dhakeswari Temple were evicted forcefully by the political and communal forces. Out of 20 (twenty) Bighas of land endowed absolutely to the Deity, 3.14 acres of land were recorded in the CS Plots No. 30 and 41 pertaining to CS Khatian No. 16795 under police station-Kotwali, Dhaka City Mouja of Jahangir Nagar Pargana in Dhaka District in the name of one Chatradhari Koiri, son of late Ram Charan of Dhakeswari, who was one of the Mudis and Servicemen Proja and in the said Khatian it was clearly written that he had no right, title and possession and his name was recorded fraudulently with malafide intention although the property was Debottar Property. 

 8. By filing supplementary affidavit, the petitioners further state that while the Cadastral Survey (CS) took place, Deity's land measuring an area of 6.45 acres equivalent to 20 (Twenty) Bighas (Approx.) were recorded in the CS khatians No..16790 (Plot No. 37 & 42), 16791 (Plot No. 33), 16791 (w) (Plot No.40), 16792 (Plot No. 38), 16793 (Plot No. 39), 16794, 16795 (Plot No. 30 & 41), 16796 (Plot No. 31, 32, 34, & 35), 16797, 16798, 16799 (Plot No. 31, 32, 34, & 35), 16800 (Plot No. 31, 32, 34, & 35), 16801 (Plot No. 36) and 16802 (Plot No. 43). The land were Butted and Bounded by the then Government with Concrete (Pucca) pillars and the entire 20 Bighas of property including the schedule property were recorded in the name of Sebayet and other Mudis and/or Service men Proja on behalf of the Deity, Petitioner No.1 as the Dhakeswari Mata alias Oshttabhuja Mata alias Gangadavbya Mata alias Purnabhuja Mata alias Dashabhuja Mata etc. 

 9. On 25th April 1953, the Government of the then Pakistan, acquired part of the said CS Plot No. 30 and full portion of CS Plot No. 41 pertaining to CS Khatian No. 16795 totaling 2.56 acres of land, i.e., 2.35 acres from CS Plot No.30 and 0.21 acres from CS Plot No.41 (schedule property) vide LA Case No. 2 of 1952-53 dated April 25, 1953 Order No. 5177 under the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (the Act, 1948) for establishment of a private motor vehicle workshop in the name of respondent No. 10, M/s Momin Motor Works Ltd. The notification dated 25-4-1953 relating to schedule property was subsequently published at page No. 457 of the Dacca Gazette, May 28, 1953. Out of the above mentioned acquired land of CS Plot No. 30, only 2.23 acres of land were recorded in the SA Record in the name of Respondent No. 10, i.e., M/s Momin Motor Works Ltd., being SA Plot No. 117 pertaining to SA Khatian No. 45 under police station and mouja-Lalbagh, Dhaka District. 

 11. In the meantime, respondent No. 9, the Chairman of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha (RAJUK) vide its Gazette dated 2-2-2009 enlisted the Dhakeswari Temple as one of the special Archeological sites of Bangladesh in serial No. 20. The properties mentioned in the CS Khatian No. 16795, which are Plot Nos. 30 and 41, both are part of the Debottar Property endowed to the Petitioner No. 1, the Deity and therefore, the requisition to acquire the property by the respondents No. 6 and 8 for the establishment of the workshop of the Respondent No. 10, i.e., M/s Momin Motor Works Ltd. violates the provisions of the Act. 1948. Hence, the notification dated 25- 4-1953 relating to LA Case No. 2 of 1952-53 which was subsequently published in the Dacca Gazette dated 28-5-1953 (Annexure-C) is liable to be declared as null and void ab-initio and is of no legal effect. 

 17. The Managing Director, M/s Momin Motor Works Ltd. as respondent No.10 has also filed an affidavit in opposition contending, inter cilia, are that Dhakeswari Mondir is a Temple and the Deity therein existing for years within 1.5682 acres of land in City Survey Khatian and it is bounded by the BUET Staff Quarter in the West, Residential Houses of different peoples in the North, in the East BUET Teachers Quarter and in the South M/s Momin Motor Works Ltd. and the Government road. The claimed property appertained to Bhawal Estate is denied and that alleged "Vogartho Kabuliyat" did not convey any title and it does not attract any identifiable land. The Mahanagar Puja Committee does not have any authority to deal with the property of the Deity. The land of the Deity has been recorded in the name of Deity. The case land is in the enjoyment and possession of this answering respondent for more than 70 years exclusively in its own right. Hence, the alleged claim is barred by limitation. 

 i. The subject property bearing plots No. 30 (part) and 41 appertaining to CS Khatian No. 16795 refers to CS Khatian No. 16794 and it shows the owner of the property was Lakheraj Gongadebba which is in other words "Dhakeswari Mata", a place of worship of the Hindu Religion Community. 

 5. Drawing our attention to the relevant Khatians, it has been submitted that the Khatian No. 16794 does not reflect any CS plot except for referring to Khatian No. 16795 containing the plots of the acquired land. In the Khatian No. 16794, superior holder was Lakheraj Ganga-debba and showing the name, Nur Box as possessor for a limited period. Thus, Khatian No. 16795 was prepared mentioning acquired plots in the name of temporary tenant, Nur Box for a certain period as mentioned therein. 

 32. Undisputedly the property measuring an area of 2.56 acres land appertaining to CS Plots No. 41 and 30(part) under CS Khatian No. 16795 (hereinafter referred to as the schedule property) were initially requisitioned on 12-4-1952 under 3rd proviso to section 3 of the then East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 (the Act, 1948) in order to acquire the land permanently through LA Case No. 2 of 1952-53. Thereafter, on observance of required process under section 5 of the Act, 1948, the schedule property was acquired and finally Gazette Notification was published on 28-5-1953 (notification dated 25-4-1953) for the Requiring Body M/s Momin Motor works Ltd. in accordance with section 5(7) of the Act, 1948. Accordingly, the schedule property was handed over to the Requiring Body for establishing a Motor Workshop in the acquired Land. Later on, the Government again acquired 1.75 acres from the said acquired Land belonged to the Requiring Body, M/s Momin Motor works Ltd. through LA Case No. 8 of 1982-83 in favour of the Requiring Body, the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) by Gazette publication dated 6-10-1994 and upon handing over possession thereof. The BUET is now enjoying the property constructing building and other structures. 

 43. However, Mr. Siddique has drawn our attention to the CS Khatians as annexed in "Y" series to the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioners and he submits that CS Khatians No. 16794 and 16795 have to be read and considered together by which it shows that Lakheraj Gongadebba was superior holder through possession by one Prahallat Muhant Wary under the superior land lord. One Nurbox was tenant for certain period under whom Chatradahi Kohory was also tenant regarding the land in question. Thus the petitioners claim title and possession of the Deity in the schedule property pursuant to CS records being plots No. 41 and 30 (part) under CS khatian No. 16795. 

 44. But disputing this claim, Mr. Garib-e-Newaz, learned Advocate for the respondent No.10 submits that the acquired plots attracted latest Khatian being No. 16795 and it reflects the superior land lord was Nurbox who got it under section 106 and 108(A) of the Bengal Tenancy Act (BT Act) through auction purchase. Nurbox being tenancy holder engaged the Chatradhari Koiry in the land in question under rent for Tk. 40/-. Further, learned Advocate has drawn our attention to the Annexure-1 to the supplementary affidavit filed by the respondents No. 16-18, a sale Certificate of the Civil Decree Suit No. 75 of 1929 corresponding to Suit No. 20 of 2018 by which learned Advocate submits that after CS survey the property was sold in auction in execution of a Court decree against Prahallat Muhant Wary and others and in the execution case one Gokul Chandra Roy became the auction purchaser. He has drawn our attention to the following schedule from the order sheet of Civil Decree suit No. 75 of 1929 which runs as follows:— 

 46. Although, Mr. Siddique assails this fact drawing our attention to the CS Khatian showing that the property was settled without rent and, as such, question of rent suit does not arise. But these are the Certified Copies of the Court Proceedings showing auction purchase, which definitely require to be disapproved by proper adjudication. 

 49. Inspite of above scenerio, since by referring to the CS Khatians learned Advocate for the petitioners claims title of the Deity in the acquired property, we are of the view that the writ petition involves a disputed question of facts to be ascertained as to whether before acquisition, the property belonged to the Deity and used for religious worship. Unless it is settled, we are not inclined to adjudicate the legal issue under this Rule Nisi as to the propriety of acquisition made by the respondent-Government under LA case No. 2 of 1952-53 in accordance with sections 3 and 5 of the Act, 1948. In the circumstances, before challenging the acquisition, the petitioners need to institute a properly framed suit before the competent civil Court of jurisdiction to establish the fact that before acquisition the petitioner Deity had title and possession in the schedule property and that the same was used by the public for the purpose of religious worship.
